dedupe_keys.name: eu maritime profile section 4 environment emsa

description: The environment section of the EU Maritime Profile, published by the European Maritime Safety Agency, gives data on emissions from ships in the EU: greenhouse gases, air pollutants, underwater radiated noise and water discharges, with statistics on inspections for low sulphur fuel use, compliance with sulphur rules by region and the use of low-emission fuels and alternative technologies. It reports verified MRV emissions (CO2 in 2023 was 7.9% below 2022 and about 13% below 2018 and 2019, with 2019 the highest year on record and an 11.9% fall in 2020) and modelled emissions for all shipping around the EU from the Ship Traffic Emission Assessment Model (STEAM) of the Finnish Meteorological Institute, which are not directly comparable. Using the UNFCCC inventory, shipping was 13.4% of EU transport CO2 in 2023 and 5.5% of total EU CO2. Coverage: EU waters and EU-related voyages. Format and access: web charts and tables, without registration. Licence and cost: free under EMSA website terms. Caveats: indicators mix reported and modelled sources and change with UK withdrawal and MRV scope. It supports climate and capacity planning studies of ports and shipping. It relates to the THETIS-MRV and THETIS port state control records and, for aviation, the ICAO engine emissions databank in the catalogue.
